title: Calibration snapshot playback and answer-consistency regression harness for INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Priya Raman
description: Objective: Build a reproducible regression harness that replays captured calibration snapshots across GPTQ and AWQ weight-only INT8 conversion flows and validates answer-level consistency against a golden canonical set. Motivation: numeric sanity and distributional checks are necessary but insufficient; we need a lightweight nightly that can detect subtle functional regressions (hallucination rate, tokenization drift, and ranking flips) introduced by calibration changes, kernel selection or FP8->INT8 pipeline diffs. This ticket implements the snapshot-playback pipeline, acceptance metrics, CI jobs, and an associated dashboard and alerting rules.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration snapshot schema v1 stored in s3://redwood-quant-calibration/snapshots/{model}/{snapshot_id}.json and retrievable by job id
CI job ci/quant/snapshot-playback-smoke runs on PRs and completes within 30m for fast models (<= 1B params), returning pass/fail status
Nightly job ci/quant/answer-consistency-nightly runs full matrix (GPTQ/AWQ, HW backends) and uploads metrics to observability dashboard with historical retention
Defined thresholds: token-EM delta <= 0.6% absolute, BLEU/ROUGE degrade <= 1.5% relative, embedding cosine mean delta <= 0.01, and >0.5% ranking flips trigger investigation
Automatic artifact linkage: failed runs upload model outputs, diff logs, calibration snapshot id, and links to PRs/commits
Playbacks support deterministic seeding for RNG and can replay KV-cache priming sequences
Rollback guidance documented in playbook with clear action steps for canary vs full rollback
technical_notes: Snapshot contents: per-layer activation histograms (buckets), per-channel scale factors, representative input prefixes, tokenizer version, model commit hash, and RNG seed
Playback harness will emulate the same tokenization and prefixing used at capture time; tokenizer diffs are treated as a separate failure class
We will instrument an "answer-similarity" metric combining token-level EM, normalized-lm log-prob shifts, and embedding-cosine to reduce false positives
For AWQ: include clamping/zero-point artifacts in snapshot and ensure quantizer config parity during playback
Execution variants: CPU fallback, CUDA fp16 kernels, and cuquantized int8 kernels; the job matrix will assert functional equivalence where performance permits
We will pin a small golden seed set (~250 prompts) drawn from production prompt families for smoke, and a larger suite (~4k) for nightly longrun
Add lightweight permutation tests to detect non-deterministic regressions caused by scheduling changes
test_plan: Local dev: play back 10 calibration snapshots against GPTQ and AWQ build artifacts; verify outputs are stable for deterministic seeds
PR gating: run ci/quant/snapshot-playback-smoke with 50-sample smoke set on each PR touching quantization, runtime, or kernel selection; reports must be green
Nightly: ci/quant/answer-consistency-nightly runs full matrix across 3 hardware profiles and uploads results to metrics-db with retention 90 days
Chaos run: weekly chaos job that injects small timing jitter and runs playback to detect ordering-sensitive flakiness
Alerting: PagerDuty on >2 failing models or a single model exceeding thresholds for 3 consecutive nights
Manual verification flow: when a model fails, run auxiliary evals (toxicity, safety, and high-recall QA) to triage false positives
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-02-20: prefer deterministic seeding in playback over statistical reconstruction; reduces flakiness and simplifies triage
Decision 2025-02-24: include tokenizer version in snapshot; tokenization mismatch will be classified as 'tokenizer-drift' not quantization failure
Trade-off: larger snapshot payloads (per-channel histograms) increase S3 costs but catch more corner-cases; accepted for nightly runs, trimmed for PR smoke
